verbalization: Bremelanotide is shown to have a target relationship with Inosine-5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase 1 through two distinct pathways. In one pathway, Bremelanotide acts on the IgG receptor FcRn large subunit p51, which is targeted by (2S)-2-Amino-4-((carboxycarbonyl)amino)butanoic acid, a compound that in turn targets Inosine-5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase 1. In the second pathway, Bremelanotide directly targets Calu-1, which is targeted by Schottenol, also leading to the inhibition of Inosine-5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase 1. Both pathways suggest that Bremelanotide may exert its effects through a mechanism that involves the inhibition of Inosine-5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase 1, potentially through the modulation of its target receptors or through direct interaction with the enzyme itself. The evidence supports a mechanistic link between Bremelanotide and Inosine-5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase 1, though the exact mode of action remains to be fully elucidated.
